content:
Apple has just released the RC version of iOS 26.6 and related updates. The company's official release notes confirm that a new feature will be added to help users prepare their iPhones in advance for the upgrade to iOS 27.

Apple will begin Spotlight indexing work starting with iOS 26.6, getting your iPhone ready in advance for iOS 27.

It is rare for Apple to explicitly mention future software updates in its new release notes.

But this is exactly what happened after the release of the iOS 26.6 RC.

Below is the official release notes for iOS 26.6:

Given that the beta version revealed almost no new features, iOS 26.6 is essentially comprised of bug fixes and security updates, which is in line with our expectations.

However, the mention of Spotlight indexing is quite interesting.

Last month, when the iOS 27 beta was first released, developers discovered that their iPhones were continuously performing indexing work for an extended period. For many users, the indexing process took a week or even longer.

Apple clearly does not want the average user to experience the same situation when iOS 27 officially launches this autumn.

Therefore, the company has chosen to complete most of the indexing work ahead of time in iOS 26.6, laying the groundwork for a smoother experience with iOS 27.

So if you notice your iPhone performing Spotlight indexing after installing iOS 26.6, there is a reason for it—the all-new Siri and Spotlight improvements in iOS 27 will benefit from this preparatory work.
